[Draft] feat(perf): add support for embedding and rerank models (#1140)

* feat(perf): add support for embedding and rerank models

Add new API plugins and dataset plugins for embedding and rerank model
performance testing:

New API plugins:
- openai_embedding_api: Support for OpenAI-compatible embedding endpoints
- openai_rerank_api: Support for OpenAI-compatible rerank endpoints

New dataset plugins:
- random_embedding: Random text generation for embedding testing
  - Supports min_prompt_length and max_prompt_length parameters
  - Default range: 10-256 characters (suitable for embedding models)
- random_embedding_batch: Batch embedding testing with configurable batch_size
- random_rerank: Random query-document pair generation for rerank testing
  - Supports num_documents parameter via extra_args
  - Note: Does NOT support prompt size configuration (uses fixed sample texts)

Modified files:
- benchmark.py: Integration for new model types
- benchmark_util.py: Metric calculation updates for embedding/rerank
- db_util.py: Database schema updates for new metrics
- rich_display.py: Display formatting for new model types

subject: [Fix] Use seeded random.Random for dataset shuffling (#1243)
message:
[Fix] Use seeded random.Random for dataset shuffling (#1243)

* [Fix] Use seeded random.Random for dataset shuffling (Python 3.12+ compat)

Python 3.12 removed the deprecated second argument from random.shuffle().
LocalDataLoader.load() and DictDataLoader.load() both passed self.seed as
the second argument, causing TypeError on Python 3.12+.

Replace with random.Random(seed).shuffle(dataset) when a seed is provided,
falling back to unseeded random.shuffle() when seed is None.

RemoteDataLoader is unaffected (uses HuggingFace Dataset.shuffle(seed=...)).

Added tests/test_loader_shuffle.py covering seeded shuffle, unseeded shuffle,
reproducibility, and a guard confirming the original call fails on 3.12+.

subject: fix(perf): stabilise realised QPS in open-loop / rate-paced benchmarks (#1367)
message:
fix(perf): stabilise realised QPS in open-loop / rate-paced benchmarks (#1367)

* fix: keep stable QPS in open-loop rate mode

Pre-compute a cumulative dispatch schedule once per phase and sleep until
each absolute target time, so event-loop jitter is absorbed instead of
accumulating into a monotonic drift of the realised QPS. Mirrors the
approach used by vllm/benchmarks/benchmark_serving.py.
Affects OpenLoopStrategy._run_phase and ClosedLoopStrategy._run_phase
(rate != -1 path only). The unrate-capped path is unchanged.

Auto-install uvloop's EventLoopPolicy on POSIX when importable, falling
back to the default selector loop otherwise. Adds uvloop as a soft
dependency under the existing `perf` extra and exposes
EVALSCOPE_DISABLE_UVLOOP as an escape hatch.
Reduces per-iteration scheduling jitter under high concurrency, which
tightens the realised QPS around the configured --rate when paired with
the absolute-time dispatcher.

Closes #1366

* refactor(perf): pre-compute absolute dispatch timestamps in rate-paced loops

   Address bot review feedback: hoist `delay_ts + time.perf_counter()` out
   of the per-iteration sleep computation so each dispatch step does only
   a single index lookup + subtraction, instead of an addition plus a
   float() cast. Behaviour is unchanged; this aligns the dispatch shape
   more closely with vllm/benchmarks/benchmark_serving.py and tightens
   per-iteration scheduling overhead.

* refactor(perf): move install_uvloop_if_available to utils/handler.py

- Move uvloop event loop policy helper from main.py to utils/handler.py
  where other event-loop infrastructure (signal handlers) already lives.
- Rename _install_uvloop_if_available -> install_uvloop_if_available (public API).
- Add test_rate_stability.py: unit tests verifying absolute-time scheduling
  keeps realised QPS within 15% of configured rate (all 7 tests pass).

subject: fix(agent/sandbox): fail-fast in EnclaveAgentEnvironment when ms_enclave is missing (#1372)
message:
fix(agent/sandbox): fail-fast in EnclaveAgentEnvironment when ms_enclave is missing (#1372)

EnclaveAgentEnvironment hardcodes ms_enclave for all sandbox engines
(docker / volcengine / enclave). Previously the dependency was only
checked when TaskConfig.sandbox.enabled=True, so users running agentic
benchmarks (e.g. swe_bench_*_agentic, swe_bench_pro_agentic) without
'evalscope[sandbox]' silently got 0.0 scores: every bash tool call
raised ImportError('No module named ms_enclave'), the agent loop
returned that as a tool error, and the model spent 250 steps complaining
about a broken environment until the adapter wrote reasoning text into
patch.diff and git apply failed.

Move the check_import('ms_enclave') call into EnclaveAgentEnvironment
__init__ instead of duplicating it across each agentic adapter. This
covers every current and future caller of EnclaveAgentEnvironment with a
single fail-fast at the first sample's environment construction.

Refs #1362

* add GAIA benchmark with ReAct + bash agent

- Sandbox: python:3.11 with attachment files mounted at /shared_files

  parts no longer leak Python repr into scorer input
- Docs: third_party/gaia.md + index.md cross-link
- Smoke test: tests/benchmark/test_agent.py::test_gaia

* fix(agent): handle context-window overflow as stop_reason=model_length

Mirrors inspect_ai's three-layer design so that a single sample hitting the
model's max input length no longer aborts the entire evaluation.

Provider layer (Fix A): openai_handle_bad_request now also matches by error
message content — DashScope/vLLM/etc. surface overflow under generic codes
(e.g. DashScope: code='invalid_parameter_error', "Range of input length
should be ..."), so the existing OpenAI-only e.code check missed them and
the BadRequestError propagated up. Added "input length" / "maximum context
length" / "context window" / "too many tokens" pattern fallback.

AgentLoop layer (Fix B): after each generate, check
output.stop_reason == 'model_length' and break the loop gracefully via a new
_emit_context_overflow trace event. Compaction / message-trimming recovery
(cf. inspect_ai _handle_overflow) is intentionally out of scope.

Test: removed the temporary ignore_errors=True from test_gaia and reduced
limit to 1 sample/level for faster iteration. End-to-end run with 3 levels
now completes without errors; report shows OVERALL 0.4 (level1 0.4,
level2 0.8, level3 0.0).

Web UI: rendered the new model_context_overflow event identifier through
trace.loopMessage i18n table (en + zh) so users see "Model context window
exceeded" / "超出模型上下文窗口" instead of the raw snake_case identifier.
Same treatment applied to existing max_steps_exceeded / no_tool_call_reminder
events for consistency.

* feat(agent): MCP server support via NativeAgentConfig.mcp_servers

Lets users plug arbitrary MCP servers into any AgentLoopAdapter-based
benchmark without benchmark-side code changes — covers fetch, search,
filesystem, github and the rest of the MCP ecosystem from one entry
point. Mirrors the inspect_ai design (transport per server, tools merged
into the loop, lifecycle bound to per-sample inference).

New module evalscope/api/agent/mcp/:
- types.py: MCPServerConfigStdio / MCPServerConfigHTTP discriminated union
- client.py: async MCPServer context manager wrapping mcp.ClientSession,
  supporting stdio (StdioServerParameters) and Streamable HTTP transports
- source.py: mcp_tools(server) → (handlers_map, [ToolInfo]); converts the
  MCP inputSchema into evalscope's ToolParams shape
- __init__.py: re-exports

Wiring:
- NativeAgentConfig.mcp_servers: List[MCPServerConfig]
- run_agent_loop gains mcp_configs kwarg; opens each server inside an
  AsyncExitStack before the loop, merges tool handlers + ToolInfo into
  the dicts passed to ToolExecutor, closes everything on exit.
- AgentLoopAdapter._on_inference reads agent_config.mcp_servers and
  forwards. Other NativeAgentConfig fields stay benchmark-owned.

Soft dependency:
- requirements/mcp.txt + pyproject [mcp] extra
- mcp SDK is imported lazily inside MCPServer.__aenter__; configurations
  with empty mcp_servers (the default) need no extra install.

Tests:
- tests/agent/test_mcp.py: spawns a FastMCP echo server fixture
  (tests/agent/mcp_echo_server.py) over stdio, verifies list/call/filter.
- tests/benchmark/test_agent.py::test_gaia_with_mcp adds an integration
  smoke that wires GAIA + mcp-server-fetch; not part of the fast CI path.

* test(mcp): switch test_gaia_with_mcp to python -m mcp_server_fetch

Two practical issues hit when running the integration test:

1. ``uvx mcp-server-fetch`` is a per-call package-fetch + temp-venv
   create, which on slow PyPI links (no working mirror env vars) blocked
   the test on cryptography/lxml downloads for 5+ minutes. Swap to a
   plain ``python -m mcp_server_fetch`` once ``pip install
   mcp-server-fetch`` has put the package in the eval venv — zero
   per-test startup overhead.

2. mcp-server-fetch defaults to checking ``robots.txt`` before each
   fetch; on intermittent network access (or CDN-blocked UAs) the
   robots.txt request fails and every tool call returns ``[error]
   Failed to fetch robots.txt``. Pass ``--ignore-robots-txt`` so the
   server attempts the actual URL.

End-to-end verified with qwen3-max + GAIA level1: server initialised,
17 fetch calls, agent submitted an answer through the MCP tool path.
Score 0 (target "17" vs prediction "17000") is the same model-side
unit-comprehension issue seen in the bash-only test_gaia run, not an
MCP plumbing bug.

Also picks up two yapf cosmetic blank-line removals in the MCP module.

* docs: MCP server configuration guide + GAIA usage example

Adds a framework-level "MCP server tools" section to the Native Agent
Loop guide (en + zh) covering install / quick start / per-field
reference / trace+debugging notes, including stdio + HTTP transports
and the python -m vs uvx tradeoff.

Adds a focused "Adding web access via MCP" section to the GAIA docs
(en + zh) showing the concrete mcp-server-fetch wiring (with
--ignore-robots-txt) that lets the bash-only sandbox gain real web
access without an image rebuild — directly addressing the "no
web_search" limitation flagged in this benchmark's known-limitations.

* chore(mcp): bundle mcp-server-fetch in the [mcp] extra

Make `pip install evalscope[mcp]` "batteries-included" for the most
commonly demoed MCP server. mcp-server-fetch is the natural starter:

The starter-pack philosophy stops at one package — other MCP servers

feat(benchmarks): add k2/kimi/minimax vendor verifier benchmarks (#1375)

* feat(benchmarks): add k2/kimi/minimax vendor verifier benchmarks

Adds three benchmarks for checking whether third-party API deployments
faithfully reproduce official model behavior:

- k2_verifier: tool-calling deployment correctness against MoonshotAI's
  K2-Thinking baseline (trigger_similarity, schema_accuracy). Dataset:
  evalscope/K2VendorVerifier (2000 rows).
- kimi_verifier: synthetic pre-flight probe that checks Kimi K2 immutable
  parameter enforcement (temperature/top_p/presence_penalty/frequency_penalty/n).
  No external dataset; 55 in-memory probes across kimi/opensource/none subsets.
- minimax_verifier: multi-validator deployment check with per-row check_type
  routing (tool_calls + always-on error_only_reasoning + language_following +
  repeat_ngram + scenario_check). Dataset: evalscope/MiniMaxVendorVerifier
  (102 rows).

Shared base VendorVerifierAdapter (under api/benchmark/adapters/) lifts
JSON-schema tool-call validation, error-only-reasoning detection, and the
default chat-completion inference loop out of general_fc so all four
benchmarks can reuse them. general_fc is refactored to inherit from the new
base; no behavior change.

AGENTS.md gains a "Docs generation" section documenting the make
docs-pipeline / docs-generate workflow, since benchmark detail pages and
_meta cache are now auto-generated from BenchmarkMeta.description.

* fix(benchmarks/verifier): address PR #1375 reviewer comments

Three real bugs surfaced by the bot reviewers:

1. ModelOutput.from_content was called without the required `model`
   positional arg in both the shared base and kimi_verifier. The exception
   path would have raised TypeError instead of producing the intended
   error-output. Pre-existing bug inherited from general_fc's old impl;
   now fixed everywhere by passing `model=model.name`.

2. has_no_repeated_ngram was O(L²) (text.count called inside an outer
   loop over every position). For the ~340k-char prompts in the MiniMax
   dataset that's ~10^11 operations and would timeout. Rewritten to a
   single sliding-window Counter pass + targeted text.count verification
   on candidates only; preserves the upstream non-overlapping count
   semantics. Verified ~24 ms on 200k chars.

3. kimi_verifier's `was_rejected` flag was driven by `bool(output.error)`,
   which meant transport errors (5xx / 429 / timeout) were silently counted
   as legitimate parameter rejections, inflating param_immutable_reject_rate
   for flaky vendors. Now _on_inference catches openai.BadRequestError
   specifically (the real 400 reject signal) and tags transport errors with
   stop_reason='unknown'; match_score excludes those probes from both
   reject/accept denominators and surfaces them via a new
   `inference_error_rate` metric.

Yapf re-formatted _validators.py / minimax_verifier_adapter.py during
make lint (cosmetic).

- MultiTurnStrategy unpacks Turn: sleeps tool_call_latency before each turn,
  overrides request['max_tokens'] when per-turn cap is set, and tags every
  BenchmarkData with trace_id + is_first_turn for downstream trace-level
  aggregation
- --duration wall-clock budget honored in all three benchmark modes
  (closed-loop, open-loop, multi-turn) via a shared
  BenchmarkStrategy._gather_with_deadline helper. Warmup phases ignore
  --duration; in-flight requests are hard-cancelled at the deadline
  (trie-compatible semantics)

Tests:
- 8 unit tests for trace -> Conversation mapping (no FS / no network)
- 5 phase-barrier tests adapted to Turn shape
- 3 new duration hard-cancel tests (one per strategy)
- 1 new trace_id + is_first_turn assertion test
- 1 e2e smoke test against DashScope using real ModelScope download
  (skipped when DASHSCOPE_API_KEY is unset)

Note on numerical alignment: trie uses /v1/completions with raw prompts;
evalscope multi-turn uses /v1/chat/completions, so the server-side chat
template adds 10-20 tokens of overhead per turn. Cache-hit rate and
prompt-token counts will differ from trie by a few percent.

* fix(perf): address reviewer feedback on PR #1374

- Cap rate-pacing sleep at remaining time-to-deadline in closed/open loop
  strategies so dispatchers don't oversleep the --duration cutoff.
- Guard MultiTurnStrategy._worker against build_request() returning None
  (abandon the conversation instead of crashing).
- Catch TypeError alongside KeyError/ValueError when parsing trie traces
  so malformed list fields don't abort the whole run.
- Tighten type hints: deadline: float = None -> Optional[float] = None
  in closed_loop, open_loop, multi_turn _run_phase signatures.

* feat(perf): split TTFT into first-turn vs subsequent-turn buckets

Multi-turn benchmarks blend cold prefill (first turn) and warm prefix-cache
hits (later turns) into a single TTFT average, which hides the most
operationally meaningful effect of prefix-cache reuse.

- MetricsAccumulator now buckets TTFT by BenchmarkData.is_first_turn for
  turns with input_num_turns > 0; single-turn benchmarks leave both
  counters at 0 so the cold/warm distinction stays meaningful only when
  multi-turn data is present.
- BenchmarkMetrics surfaces avg_first_turn_ttft / avg_subsequent_turn_ttft
  (seconds internally), converted to ms in create_message().
- BenchmarkSummary exposes both as optional Pydantic fields and renders
  them in the Multi-turn section of to_table().

* feat(perf): per-trace metrics summary for multi-turn benchmarks

Adds TraceAccumulator + TraceLevelSummary so multi-turn / trace-replay
runs report per-trace aggregates that match the upstream trie reporting
format, in addition to the existing per-request metrics.

Metrics (one row each, aggregated mean / min / p50 / p90 / p95 / p99 / max
across all traces in the run):
- Latency (s)              : last_turn.completed_time - first_turn.start_time
- First-Turn TTFT (s)      : TTFT of the first turn (cold prefill)
- TTFAT (s)                : wall-clock from trace start to the first token
                             of the final assistant reply
- Decode TPS               : arithmetic mean over the trace's turns of
                             (completion_tokens-1) / (latency-ttft)
- Cache Hit Rate (%)       : sum(cached_tokens) / sum(prompt_tokens)
- Eligible Cache Hit Rate  : sum(cached_tokens) / sum(eligible) where
                             eligible_i = prev_prompt + prev_completion

Single-turn benchmarks (no trace_id) contribute nothing; the summary is
empty and downstream rendering is skipped, leaving single-turn output
unchanged.  statistic_benchmark_metric now returns
(metrics, trace_summary, db_path); callers in benchmark.py /
multi_turn_benchmark.py / summary_result thread the new value through.

* chore(perf): drop unused Optional import in trace_metrics

* feat(perf): workload-level throughput timeline (Overall / Last-window / Steady-state)

Adds WorkloadTimeline + WorkloadThroughput so multi-turn / trace-replay
runs report throughput under the three windows trie publishes:

  - Overall:      cumulative tokens / wall_time
  - Last <N>s:    sliding tail window (default 30s; falls back to Overall
                  when the run is shorter than the window)
  - Steady-state: drop the first warmup_frac (default 20%) of wall_time
                  to exclude the prefix-cache / batch-scheduler ramp

Four metrics per window: Total Prompt / New Prompt / Cached Prompt /
Completion tok/s.  The cache split derives from BenchmarkData.cached_tokens
already populated by MultiTurnStrategy; new_prompt is clamped to >= 0
because some OpenAI-compatible backends post-tokenize prompts in a way
that lets cached exceed prompt.

Storage choice: cumulative-token points live in memory and are written to
workload_timeline.json (pandas-friendly raw points) plus
workload_throughput.json (aggregated table).  The SQLite layer is left
untouched - persisting raw turn-level cache columns is a separate
refactor and shouldn't ride in this PR.

statistic_benchmark_metric now returns 4-tuple (metrics, trace_summary,
workload_timeline, db_path); both single-turn and multi-turn benchmark
entry points pass the timeline through to summary_result.  Single-turn
runs also benefit - the steady-state column factors out the cold-start
ramp that the simple "tokens / wall_time" average smears.

* refactor(perf): self-review fixes on workload_timeline

- Lock wall_start on first feed (was using min()).  Already-appended points
  carry t = completed_time - wall_start; lowering wall_start later silently
  invalidated those offsets because they're never rewritten.  Worker-race
  reordering at the queue boundary makes the bug real but sub-second.
  Added test_wall_start_locked_on_first_feed to pin the behaviour.
- Collapse _rates' five parameters into a single _Point anchor; overall /
  last-window / steady-state now share one code path with a module-level
  _ORIGIN sentinel for the Overall case.  ~40 LOC removed.
- Drop unused ConfigDict / populate_by_name=True from WorkloadThroughputRow
  (no aliases are declared).
- WorkloadThroughput.to_dict() now delegates to model_dump() instead of
  hand-listing fields.
- Trim unused WorkloadThroughput import from metrics_consumer.

* refactor(perf): soft-exit on --duration (trace-level for multi-turn)

trie's reference implementation lets already in-flight work finish past
the duration deadline; it only stops *starting* new work.  evalscope's
hard cancel was a P1 oversight - it produces partial traces in the
trace_summary table because a long trace that's halfway through its
turns at the deadline gets sliced down to whatever turns happened to
have completed.  That made TTFAT / latency / cache-hit numbers in
trace_summary noticeably noisier than trie's, even on identical inputs.

Changes per strategy:

  - ClosedLoopStrategy / OpenLoopStrategy: the dispatch loop already
    breaks on deadline; replace the hard-cancel `_gather_with_deadline`
    with a plain `asyncio.gather(...)` so already in-flight requests
    finish naturally.
  - MultiTurnStrategy: worker checks deadline at the *trace boundary*
    only.  Once a conversation is claimed, every remaining turn runs
    to completion (matches trie's `_run_workload`).  trace_summary
    therefore only contains fully completed traces.
  - Drop now-unused `_gather_with_deadline` from BenchmarkStrategy.

Test updates:
  - Rename docstrings / assertion messages from "hard-cancel" to "stop
    new dispatch / soft exit".
  - TestMultiTurnDurationCancel now asserts the trace-completeness
    invariant: every trace_id that produced any turn produced *all*
    of its turns (no partial traces).

* feat(perf): render trace summary + workload throughput as rich tables

Both tables already land in the log via tabulate, but they sit above the
final "Performance Test Summary Report" panel so a user reading the
report from the bottom up misses them.  Surface them inside the rich
report next to "Request Metrics" so the multi-turn / trace-replay
information sits where readers actually look.

Plumbing changes:
  - summary_result now returns a 4-tuple
    (summary, percentiles, trace_summary, throughput); previous callers
    in benchmark.py / multi_turn_benchmark.py pass the new fields through.
  - run_one_benchmark adds 'trace_summary' / 'workload_throughput' keys
    to its result dict so they propagate into the per-run all_results
    dict that print_summary consumes.

Rendering:
  - LLMSummaryRenderer._render_extra_tables now emits a "Per-trace
    Summary" rich table (when trace data is present) and a "Workload
    Throughput" rich table (when timeline data is present), each on its
    own row.  Single-turn runs skip the trace table; runs with no
    successful requests skip throughput.
  - Sweep mode prefixes the table title with the run label so multi-row
    sweeps stay readable.

End-to-end vs upstream trie (Qwen-Plus / office_work, chat-history mode,
temperature=0): Decode TPS -1.1%, Latency +1.3%, TTFAT -4.5%, Cache hit
within 12% (residual gap is sample-size, not algorithm).

* docs(perf): add trace-replay user guide + --duration parameter docs

New page docs/{zh,en}/user_guides/stress_test/trace_replay.md covers:
  - Why the trie jsonl carries only token-length metadata (privacy /
    cross-model comparability / license hygiene) and how the client
    synthesises prompts to those lengths
  - Quick-start command, the three built-in workloads, and how to
    bring your own jsonl
  - How to read Per-trace Summary / Workload Throughput / First-Turn
    vs Subsequent-Turn TTFT — what each column means and where to
    look when it's off
  - --duration + --number pairing with soft-exit semantics
  - Backend caveats: ignore_eos support, chat-template overhead,
    synthetic-prompt character differences
  - Measured comparison vs upstream trie (qwen-plus, office_work,
    5 traces): algorithm layer aligned within +/-6%, residual gaps
    explained by trie's internal cache-hit inconsistency and
    prompt-synthesis differences

stress_test/index.md: add trace_replay.md to the toctree.
stress_test/parameters.md: document --duration (was missing from the
parameter table even though the flag landed earlier in this PR).
stress_test/multi_turn.md: add a seealso pointer to trace_replay.md
so readers landing on the multi-turn page can discover trie replay.

* fix(perf): address Copilot review feedback

- Arguments.duration docstring + --duration CLI help: was describing
  hard-cancel semantics from the original P1 design; sync with the
  trace-level soft-exit that actually shipped (deadline stops new
  dispatch but in-flight work runs to completion; in multi-turn this
  means already-claimed traces finish every remaining turn).
- DatasetPluginBase.build_messages return type was Iterator[List[Dict]]
  which lost precision once Turn / Conversation were introduced - now
  Iterator[Union[Messages, Conversation]] so type checkers / IDEs see
  the actual contract.
- WorkloadTimeline._find_anchor inline comment said "scan from the end"
  but the loop scans from the start and breaks at the first t > t_target;
  rewrite the comment to match (relies on append-only sorted-by-t
  invariant established by wall_start locking on first feed).

* refactor(docs/perf): merge trace_replay into multi_turn docs, remove redundant tests

- Merge trace_replay.md content into multi_turn.md (both en/zh) since trie
  trace replay is a multi-turn dataset, not a separate feature
- Remove trace_replay.md from toctree index
- Remove redundant unit tests (test_metrics_first_turn_split,
  test_strategies_phase_barrier, test_rate_stability) covered by e2e tests
- Remove verbose "Phase deadline set" log message from multi_turn strategy

* refactor(perf): deep cleanup rich_display architecture + add max column + update docs

Analyzer layer:
- BaseResultAnalyzer no longer ABC; only static utilities (_parse_entry, normalize, _get_p99)
- LLMResultAnalyzer.analyze() only computes aggregates, no formatted row dicts
- EmbeddingResultAnalyzer owns _sort_rows (using EmbCol keys) and _build_row

Renderer layer:
- BaseSummaryRenderer slimmed to _render_basic_info + 3 abstract methods
- EmbeddingSummaryRenderer absorbs detail table logic with EmbCol.SUCCESS_RATE.key
- Removed dead code: _detail_columns, _make_detail_table, _fill_table_rows, _render_extra_tables

Data pipeline:
- AnalysisResult gains n_entries field; print_summary checks n_entries instead of rows
- calculate_percentiles supports percentile=100 (max); percentile output adds max column
- Per-Request Metrics table adds max column (avg/p50/p99/max)

Docs:
- Updated quick_start (zh/en): new 4-table output description, restructured metric docs
- Updated multi_turn, sla_auto_tune, gpt_oss (zh/en): new table format examples

* fix lint

* fix(perf): update return type annotations and harden trie JSON parsing

- Update run_benchmark / run_multi_turn_benchmark return annotations
  from Tuple[Dict, Dict] to the actual 4-tuple shape returned by
  summary_result.
- Move json.loads inside try block in trie plugin so malformed JSON
  lines are skipped with a warning instead of aborting the load.
